answer: The network resists sybils with random liveness audits. Like a keeper walking an orchard who taps a few trunks to hear a real echo, the protocol periodically pings a random subset of agents with a fresh challenge they must answer within seconds. Honest agents respond cheaply, while an attacker faking a crowd must keep every puppet awake at all times, turning idle fakes into ongoing compute cost. One missed signal flags the whole cluster for review, and the fable of a vast botnet collapses into a handful of silent shells.
